headline: Starc takes 5 wickets, sets two world records as Bangladesh reel at 12/5 on Day 1
summary: Australian pacer Mitchell Starc delivered a devastating spell, taking five quick wickets and setting two new world records on Day 1 of the second Test against Bangladesh.
details: Australia pacer Mitchell Starc left Bangladesh in tatters, taking five wickets in quick succession and setting two new world records early on Day 1 of the second and final Test at the Great Barrier Reef Arena in Mackay.

The left-arm quick removed Bangladesh opener Shadman Islam with the first delivery, marking the fourth time Starc has taken a wicket with the opening ball of a Test. He surpassed West Indies pacer Pedro Collins, who had achieved this feat three times.
Starc also moved past England great James Anderson for the most instances of taking a wicket in the first over of a Test, now with nine such dismissals, one more than Anderson.

After dismissing Shadman, Starc struck again in his second over, removing opener Tanzid Tamim and Bangladesh captain Najmul Hossain Shanto off successive deliveries, with all three batters falling for ducks.
He continued his rampage in the fifth over, having Mominul Haque edge one to Cameron Green. Starc then removed Litton Das for a five-ball duck in the following over.

Starc needed just 15 balls to complete his 19th Test five-for, claiming the fastest five-wicket haul in Test cricket history. This bettered the previous record of 17 deliveries held by fellow Australian Ernie Toshack against India in 1947.
After seven overs, Bangladesh were reeling at 12 for 5. Australia had won the toss and elected to field first in the match.
Bangladesh leads the two-match series 1-0, following their nine-wicket win in the first match in Darwin, which was their first-ever Test win on Australian soil.

A series victory would be Bangladesh's first against Australia and on Australian soil. A draw in this game would also see Bangladesh take the series, becoming only the sixth visiting team to win a Test series down under.

headline_marked: [[Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as 23rd President]], 4 ministers & 2 state ministers take oath
headline: Mirza Fakhrul sworn in as 23rd President, 4 ministers & 2 state ministers take oath
summary: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has been sworn in as Bangladesh's 23rd President, alongside four new ministers and two state ministers, marking a significant cabinet reshuffle.
details: Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at Bangabhaban. The ceremony marked a pivotal moment in the nation's political landscape.
Simultaneously, four new ministers and two state ministers also took their oaths of office. This expansion and reshuffle signifies new appointments within the Tarique-led government.

The Cabinet Division subsequently issued a gazette notification, formally assigning portfolios to the newly sworn-in ministers and state ministers. This official announcement clarifies their new responsibilities.

The appointments include prominent figures such as Moin Khan and Parth, whose supporters celebrated in their respective constituencies of Narsingdi and Bhola. These local celebrations highlight public engagement with the political changes.

Following the swearing-in, President Mirza Fakhrul received congratulatory messages from international leaders, including the Presidents of India and Nepal. Prime Minister Tarique also extended his wishes for a successful tenure.
caption:
Bangladesh witnesses a major political shift as Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir takes oath as the 23rd President.

Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir was sworn in as the 23rd President of Bangladesh at Bangabhaban. The ceremony marked a pivotal moment in the nation's political landscape.

Simultaneously, four new ministers and two state ministers also took their oaths of office. This expansion and reshuffle signifies new appointments within the Tarique-led government.

The Cabinet Division subsequently issued a gazette notification, formally assigning portfolios to the newly sworn-in ministers and state ministers. This official announcement clarifies their new responsibilities.

The appointments include prominent figures such as Moin Khan and Parth, whose supporters celebrated in their respective constituencies of Narsingdi and Bhola. These local celebrations highlight public engagement with the political changes.

Following the swearing-in, President Mirza Fakhrul received congratulatory messages from international leaders, including the Presidents of India and Nepal. Prime Minister Tarique also extended his wishes for a successful tenure.
